Slices of an array

Source: R/xslices.R
xslices.Rd

xslices() lists the slices of an array that ximage() can draw: one row per combination of the non-spatial dimensions, with a column of indices for each and a "_label" column with its coordinate value where known. Only metadata is read. A row can be given to slice in ximage() and friends.

Usage

xslices(x, xy = NULL)

xpanels(
  x,
  slice = NULL,
  ...,
  zlim = NULL,
  xy = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  col = hcl.colors(96, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
  breaks = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  na.col = "transparent",
  main = NULL,
  mfrow = NULL,
  max_panels = 16L
)

Arguments

x

an array, or anything ximage() accepts

xy

the two spatial dimensions, x then y, as names or positions

slice

slices to draw, see Details

...

passed to plot for each panel

zlim

optional, absolute range of data to map colours to (maintains comparable colours across plots); values outside display as 'na.col'; single-band numeric data only

coords

optional coordinates of the spatial dimensions, list(x = , y = ) of centres, edges, or curvilinear matrices (see Details)

col

colours to map single-band data to

breaks

a set of finite numeric breakpoints for the colours, one more break than colour (if not, colours are interpolated to fit)

alpha

optional constant opacity in [0, 1] (or vector/matrix, recycled) applied on top of any existing alpha channel; not supported for nativeRaster input

na.col

colour for missing values, default "transparent"

main

panel titles, default from the slice and its label

mfrow

panel layout, default from grDevices::n2mfrow()

max_panels

the most panels drawn by default

Value

xslices() a data frame (with zero columns for data with no dimensions to slice); xpanels() invisibly, a list of what ximage() returns for each panel and the 'zlim' used

Details

xpanels() draws several slices side by side with one colour scale (the range of all the slices drawn, unless 'zlim' or 'breaks' is given), each titled by its slice. Give the slices as a list with several indices along one dimension, e.g. list(time = 1:6), or as rows of xslices() output. The default is the first slices along the first non-spatial dimension.

Examples

a <- array(c(volcano, volcano * 0.9, volcano * 0.8, volcano * 0.7),
           c(y = 87, x = 61, time = 4))
xslices(a)
#>   time
#> 1    1
#> 2    2
#> 3    3
#> 4    4
xpanels(a)

xpanels(a, slice = list(time = c(1, 4)))
